citation.title: Revised error field assessment in KSTAR with profile diagnostics of resonant field penetration
citation.authors: Seo G.-G., Han S.-J., Kim J., Lee Y., Yang S.M., Juhn J.W., Park J.-K.

topic: Assessment of the n=1 intrinsic error field in KSTAR using compass scans, with ECE and CES timing used to identify q=2 penetration.
own_question: What is the present intrinsic error-field amplitude and direction in KSTAR, and how can the local penetration time be defined?
actual_method_and_evidence: The study used 2025-campaign MID, OFFMID and H-mode compass scans, GPEC overlap-field comparison, one rotating-RMP shot and a reversed-Bt scan. The authors report that CES toroidal-rotation sampling carries a ±5 ms timing uncertainty. CES appears only as rotation profiles for offline event timing. The paper does not address temperature nowcasting, BES/ECEI estimators or KSTAR2022 data.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In a KSTAR error-field study, CES rotation and ECE were combined offline to time local q=2 events. The authors cite a ±5 ms CES sampling uncertainty.
claim_checks.qualification: This concerns rotation, not Ti, and a different campaign and purpose. It does not establish CES report latency or arrival times.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The paper uses offline post-shot event timing only. It defines no online inputs.
validation_if_relevant: The evidence is cross-configuration consistency across 8 discharges. These are not estimator validation designs.
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat ±5 ms as our CES cadence or latency.
Do not cite this paper as support for nowcasting carbon-impurity Ti.
Do not imply this paper used BES/ECEI for temperature estimation.
Do not generalize its 2025 conditions to KSTAR2022.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude, or at most cite as a minor example of offline KSTAR CES/ECE timing use. Its topic does not match our study.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
